title: MATH171: Calculus I Practice Question Bank

content.label: Limit Definition
content.text: $\lim_{x \to a} f(x) = L$ means that $f(x)$ can be made arbitrarily close to $L$ by taking $x$ sufficiently close to $a$ (but $x \neq a$).

content.label: Intermediate Value Theorem (IVT)
content.text: If $f$ is continuous on $[a, b]$ and $N$ is any value between $f(a)$ and $f(b)$, then there exists at least one $c \in (a, b)$ such that $f(c) = N$.
A function is continuous at $a$ if $\lim_{x \to a} f(x) = f(a)$. Discontinuities can be removable, jump, or infinite.

content.label: Limit Laws
content.text: $\lim_{x \to a} [f(x) \cdot g(x)] = \lim_{x \to a} f(x) \cdot \lim_{x \to a} g(x)$

content.label: Critical Points
content.text: Points where $f'(x) = 0$ or $f'(x)$ is undefined. These are candidates for local extrema.

content.label: Second Derivative Test
content.text: If $f'(c) = 0$ and $f''(c) > 0$, then $f$ has a local minimum at $c$. If $f''(c) < 0$, then $f$ has a local maximum at $c$.
The second derivative $f''(x)$ describes the concavity of the function.
Find the dimensions of a rectangular field with 400m fencing that maximizes area.
The definite integral $\int_{a}^{b} f(x) dx$ represents the net signed area under the curve.

summary: Limits describe behavior near a point, not necessarily at the point itself.
Continuity requires the limit to exist, the function to be defined, and the two to be equal.
The Chain Rule is essential for differentiating composite functions.
Critical points are found where the first derivative is zero or undefined.
The Fundamental Theorem of Calculus links differentiation and integration as inverse operations.
